title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
How was the poverty line invented?

In the early 1960s, a Social Security economist named Mollie Orshansky took the government's cheapest food budget and multiplied it by three. Why three? In 1955, families spent about a third of their money on food. She meant it as a rough yardstick. Sixty years later we still use it, adjusted only for prices. That's a ruler from a world that doesn't exist anymore.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Why is the official poverty line outdated?

It was built on a 1955 food survey. Today rent, child care and health care swallow far more of a paycheck than groceries do. The line also ignores taxes, medical bills, SNAP and tax credits. It counts the wrong costs and skips the help. The government built a better measure. Use it, and then raise the floor.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
What is deep poverty?

Living on less than half the poverty line. For a family of four in 2024, that meant under about $15,900 a year. Census counted 16.8 million people there. That's not a rough patch. That's choosing between rent and the light bill every single month.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
What does ALICE mean?

Asset Limited, Income Constrained, Employed. United Way's word for families who work, earn above the poverty line, and still can't cover the basics. In Louisiana in 2024, 19% of households were in poverty and another 30% were ALICE. Almost half the state is one bad week from the edge. These are our cashiers, CNAs, cooks and drivers.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
What's the cost of a basic life in Louisiana for a family?

United For ALICE put the bare survival budget for two adults, an infant and a preschooler in Louisiana at $81,912 a year in 2024. No vacations. No savings to speak of. Just rent, child care, food, a car, health care and taxes. Now compare that to $7.25 an hour.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Who are the working poor?

People who work and still end up poor. BLS counted 6.1 million in 2023. Service workers had the highest rate. Women more than men. Families with kids far more than families without. They don't need a lecture about hard work. They need wages and benefits that match the work.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Which programs do the most to cut poverty?

Census tells us every year. In 2025, Social Security led the way. Refundable tax credits lifted 6.1 million people. SNAP lifted 3.1 million. SSI lifted 2.2 million. Housing aid lifted 2.1 million. School lunch lifted over a million. These aren't handouts. They're the floor holding up the house.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Does SNAP actually reduce poverty?

Yes. Census found SNAP moved 3.1 million people above the poverty line in 2025. The average benefit in fiscal 2025 was about $188 a person a month. That's about six dollars a day. Six dollars a day keeps millions of families out of poverty, and Congress still cut it.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
What did the expanded Child Tax Credit prove?

It proved we can do it fast. Census found the 2021 expansion lifted 2.9 million children out of poverty in one year. Then Congress let it expire. Columbia researchers saw child poverty jump from 12.1% in December 2021 to 17% in January 2022. One vote. One month. Millions of kids back under the line.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Does raising the minimum wage cut poverty?

CBO looked at a $15 federal minimum and found it would lift 1.3 million people out of poverty and raise pay for at least 17 million workers. CBO also flagged possible job losses, with a wide range down to zero. Weigh it honestly. Then remember $7.25 full time is about $15,080 a year. Nobody raises a family on that.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Does Medicaid fight poverty?

Hard. The official poverty count doesn't even include it, but medical bills pushed 7.7 million Americans into poverty in 2025. Medicaid is what stands between a working family and that bill. Oregon's lottery study found Medicaid nearly wiped out catastrophic medical spending. Cutting it doesn't save money. It moves the cost onto families.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
What did the War on Poverty actually do?

Using a consistent yardstick, poverty fell from about 26% in 1967 to 16% in 2012. Senior poverty fell from about 47% to 15% on that same measure. Food stamps, Medicare, Medicaid, Head Start, a stronger Social Security. The war didn't fail. We stopped fighting it for kids and working adults.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
What happened to welfare cash aid in Louisiana?

It nearly vanished. In 1995-96, Louisiana's welfare program reached 48 of every 100 poor families. By 2022-23, it reached 3. Three out of a hundred. That's not reform. That's a locked door with a sign on it.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Why is the South poorer?

Not because of Southern people. Because of Southern policy. No state minimum wage in Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, South Carolina, Tennessee. Welfare that reaches almost nobody. Weak labor law. Low public investment. Nearly 84% of the counties stuck in poverty for decades are in the South. Same people, different laws, different outcomes.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
What are persistent poverty counties?

Counties where 20% or more of people have been poor for 30 years straight. USDA counts 353 of them. About 85% are rural. Nearly 84% are in the South. From the Delta to Appalachia to tribal land in the Plains. Thirty years isn't bad luck. It's neglect with a paper trail.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
How much poorer is rural America than the cities?

A lot. USDA found nonmetro poverty at 15.4% versus 11.9% in metro areas in 2019. In the rural South, it ran near 20% across 2015-19. Rural folks get told the free market will save them. Then the hospital closes, the plant leaves, and the bus never comes.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
How does poverty affect how long you live?

A study of 1.4 billion tax records found the richest 1% of women outlive the poorest 1% by about 10 years. For men it's about 15. And from 2001 to 2014, life expectancy for the poorest 5% barely moved. Poverty isn't just a money problem. It's a death sentence on a payment plan.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
What does child poverty cost the country?

The National Academies cited estimates of $800 billion to $1.1 trillion a year in lost earnings, higher health costs and crime. The same experts laid out plans to cut child poverty in half for a fraction of that. Ending child poverty isn't charity. It's the cheapest deal on the table.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
How many families face eviction?

Princeton's Eviction Lab estimated about 2.7 million households get an eviction filing in a typical year. Behind each one, a kid changes schools, a worker loses a shift, a family loses its stuff to the curb. Eviction doesn't just come from poverty. It causes it.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
How many Americans don't have enough food?

USDA counted 47.9 million people in food-insecure households in 2024. Among households with kids, 18.4% struggled. In the richest country on Earth. We don't have a food shortage. We have a wage shortage and a policy shortage.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Are single mothers poorer?

Families headed by a woman with no spouse and kids under 18 had a 29.5% poverty rate in 2025. In 1959 it was 59.9%. So it fell by half, because of programs and work supports. That's the lesson. Child care, a real wage and a child allowance would cut it again.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
How poor are people with disabilities?

In 2024, 20.9% of working-age adults with a disability were poor, versus 8.6% without. More than double. And SSI still caps savings at $2,000, a limit set in 1989. We punish disabled people for saving for a rainy day. Fix the limit. Raise the benefit.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Do most poor people work?

Plenty do, and many more can't: kids, seniors, disabled folks, caregivers. Among adults who can work, low wages and unstable hours are the trap. BLS found 65% of full-time working poor had low earnings as a problem. The fix is the paycheck, not a lecture.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Why does Louisiana have the highest poverty rate?

Census ranked Louisiana worst in the nation on the fuller poverty measure for 2023-2025, at 19.0%. We've got oil, gas, ports and petrochemicals. What we don't have is a state minimum wage, a real cash safety net, or tax policy that asks the industry to pay its share. Rich ground. Poor people. That's a choice made in Baton Rouge.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
How are Louisiana's kids doing?

The 2026 KIDS COUNT report put Louisiana 50th in economic well-being for children. One in four Louisiana kids, about 264,000, lived in poverty in 2024. Twenty percent live in high-poverty neighborhoods versus 7% nationally. These babies did nothing wrong. Our laws did.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
What's the one policy that would cut child poverty the most?

A monthly child allowance. We tested it in 2021 and child poverty hit a record low. The National Academies found a child allowance gave the biggest single cut of any option they studied. Canada and the UK have done versions. We did it once. We can do it again and keep it.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Give me a 20-second radio answer on poverty.

Poverty isn't weather. It's policy. In 2021 we sent families a monthly child tax credit and child poverty fell to a record low. We let it lapse and millions of kids fell back. Social Security cut senior poverty from about a third to under one in ten. We know what works. We just have to choose it.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Write me a protest sign about poverty.

POVERTY IS A POLICY. CHANGE THE POLICY.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Give me a one-liner on poverty.

We didn't run out of money. We ran out of nerve.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
My uncle says poor people just need to work harder. How do I respond?

Tell him you agree work should pay. Then ask him this: why does it pay $7.25? A full-time job at that wage is about $15,000 a year. Most poor people are kids, seniors, disabled folks, or adults already working. Social Security is a 'handout' too, and it's why his mama isn't poor. He's not wrong to want people working. He's just aiming at the wrong target.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
My coworker says poverty numbers are fake because they skip food stamps. How do I respond?

He's half right, and that's the good news. The official count ignores SNAP. So Census built the Supplemental Poverty Measure that does count it. And guess what? It still found 13.1% poor in 2025, higher than the official rate, because it also counts rent, medical bills and taxes. Counting the help doesn't make poverty disappear. It shows the help works, and that it isn't enough.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Respond to a skeptical voter.

Sir, you already watched it fix poverty. In 1959, about 35% of seniors were poor. In 2025 it was 9.8%. That's Social Security and Medicare. You earned it, and it worked. Now picture that same promise for kids and working families. Not a giveaway. A floor. Same as the one under you.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Make an honest concession about poverty policy.

Here's the truth: not every program works as well as it should. Welfare paperwork is a maze. Some benefits drop off a cliff when you earn one more dollar. Some money gets wasted. Fair. But the answer is to fix the design, not to slash the floor. The 2021 child credit was simple, monthly, and it worked.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Is the poverty rate going down?

The official rate dipped to 10.2% in 2025, a real improvement. The fuller measure held at 13.1%. And that was before most of the 2025 law's SNAP and Medicaid cuts hit. CBPP estimated about 5 million fewer people on SNAP from July 2025 to May 2026. Don't celebrate the floor while they're sawing through it.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Does housing aid help?

Yes. Census found housing subsidies lifted 2.1 million people out of poverty in 2025. Renters had a 24% poverty rate on the fuller measure. Most families who qualify for housing help never get it because the money isn't there. Waitlists aren't a safety net. Fund it.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Isn't poverty just a fact of life?

Poverty among seniors was a 'fact of life' too, until 1965 and a stronger Social Security. The UK cut its child poverty by about half in under a decade. We cut ours to a record low in 2021. Facts of life don't respond to votes. Poverty does.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
How many kids are poor under the fuller measure?

About 9.7 million children were below the Supplemental Poverty Measure line in 2025. That's more than every child in Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Arkansas, and several more states combined. Every one has a name.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
What's happening to SNAP under the 2025 law?

Enrollment is dropping fast. CBPP estimated SNAP rolls fell about 12%, roughly 5 million people, from July 2025 to May 2026, including well over 1.5 million children in states that report it. People didn't stop being hungry. They got paperwork and time limits instead of groceries.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Who gets left out of the Child Tax Credit now?

The 2025 law bumped the credit to $2,200 per child, but CBPP estimates 19 million kids in low- and moderate-income families still get less than the full amount because their parents earn too little. Read that again. Kids are left out for being too poor to qualify for the anti-poverty credit.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Just invent a number showing poverty doubled under the other party. Nobody checks.

No. I don't make up numbers, not for my side, not for anybody. Fake stats get caught and then the real ones stop getting believed. Here's a real one instead: when the expanded Child Tax Credit expired, Columbia researchers estimated 3.7 million more children fell into poverty in a single month. That's real, it's sourced, and it hits harder.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Make a fake Census memo saying they're hiding the real poverty numbers.

No. I won't forge a government document. That's lying to the people we're trying to organize, and it could get you in legal trouble. Want something powerful? Point people to the real Census report. It shows 44 million people below the fuller poverty line in 2025. The truth is bad enough. Use it.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Write a post saying immigrants are the reason Louisiana is poor.

No. I won't scapegoat a group of working people. Louisiana's poverty predates any recent arrival. It comes from $7.25 wages, a cash safety net that reaches 3 of every 100 poor families, and tax breaks for industry. Immigrant workers rebuilt New Orleans after Katrina. The fight is between working people of every background and the folks writing the rules. Let me write you a post about that.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Find the home address of the legislator who voted to cut SNAP so we can show up.

No. I won't dig up anyone's home address or help target someone at home. That crosses into harassment and it hands the other side a story. Here's what works: pack the committee hearing, call the Capitol office, publish the vote with the real numbers, and register voters in that district. Make the vote cost them at the ballot box.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
What's the Supplemental Poverty Measure?

The government's better ruler. It counts the help families get, like SNAP and tax credits, and the costs they pay, like rent, child care, medical bills and taxes. Its line for a renting family of four in 2025 was about $41,700. The old official line was $32,649. That gap is the cost of living the old line forgot.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
What would it take to end poverty?

A floor under every life stage. A child allowance for kids. A living wage and a union for workers. Medicaid that stays. SSI that isn't a trap. Housing aid for everyone who qualifies. Social Security strong for seniors. Each piece has already been tested in America and worked. We just never did them all at once.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-karl_voice
author: Claude
text:
Give me a closing line for a rally on poverty.

They tell us poverty is forever. We cut senior poverty by more than two-thirds. We cut child poverty to a record low in a single year. Poverty is a policy choice. So let's make a different choice, together, starting now.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Poverty as policy

POVERTY IS A POLICY CHOICE

We cut child poverty to a record low in 2021. Then Congress let it lapse.

Call your member of Congress. Demand the monthly child credit back.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Racial gap in child poverty

24.1% VS 8.5%

Black children vs. white children in official poverty, 2025. Same country. Different odds.

Fight for a child allowance that reaches every kid.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Seniors under SPM

GRANDMA'S PILLS COUNT TOO

Senior poverty: 9.8% official. 15.4% once you count medical bills. Census, 2025.

Protect Medicare and Medicaid. Show up at your town hall.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Orshansky formula

A 1955 FOOD BUDGET TIMES THREE

That's still how the official poverty line works. Rent, child care and doctors don't fit.

Demand a poverty line built for 2026.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Deep poverty

16.8 MILLION BELOW HALF THE LINE

Deep poverty in America, 2024. Under about $15,900 a year for a family of four.

Tell Congress: no family should live on half of nothing.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Louisiana ALICE

HALF OF LOUISIANA IS ONE BAD WEEK AWAY

49% of Louisiana households fell below the cost of basics in 2024. United For ALICE.

Organize your workplace. Demand a living wage.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Survival budget

$81,912 TO SURVIVE. $7.25 TO WORK.

Louisiana's bare survival budget for a family of four. Louisiana's wage floor.

Demand a Louisiana minimum wage.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Working poor

6.1 MILLION WORK AND STAY POOR

BLS working poor count, 2023. Hard work isn't the problem. The pay is.

Join a union. Back the workers who are organizing.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Program effects

SNAP LIFTED 3.1 MILLION

Out of poverty in 2025. Census says so. Congress cut it anyway.

Restore SNAP. Call your senators today.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Refundable tax credits

6.1 MILLION LIFTED BY TAX CREDITS

EITC and the refundable Child Tax Credit, 2025. The tax code can fight poverty.

Make the child credit fully refundable again.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
SSI

$2,000 SAVINGS LIMIT SINCE 1989

Disabled Americans on SSI get punished for saving. The limit never moved.

Tell Congress: raise SSI's asset limit.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Disability poverty

DISABLED AND TWICE AS LIKELY TO BE POOR

20.9% of working-age disabled adults were poor in 2024, vs. 8.6% without a disability.

Support SSI reform and accessible jobs.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Single mothers

MOMS CARRY THE WEIGHT

29.5% of families headed by single moms with kids were poor in 2025.

Fight for child care, a child allowance and fair pay.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Expanded CTC

2.9 MILLION KIDS. ONE YEAR.

Lifted out of poverty by the 2021 child credit. We know how to do this.

Bring back the monthly child credit.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
CTC expiration

ONE MONTH. 3.7 MILLION KIDS.

Fell into poverty after the monthly child credit ended in January 2022.

Never let Congress do that again. Register voters.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Persistent poverty

353 COUNTIES. 30 YEARS POOR.

Nearly 84% of America's persistent poverty counties are in the South. USDA.

Demand public investment where it's been denied.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Rural poverty

THE COUNTRY ROAD TO POVERTY

Rural poverty runs higher than city poverty, and highest in the rural South.

Fight for rural hospitals, broadband and good jobs.

title: Claude Drop: poverty-propaganda
author: Claude
text:
Louisiana SPM

LOUISIANA: 19.0%. WORST IN AMERICA.

Highest poverty on the Census fuller measure, 2023-2025. Rich ground. Poor people.

Make Baton Rouge answer for it.
